events.title: The Statute of Anne takes effect
events.description: Britain's Statute of Anne came into force. It was the first law to regulate copyright. It moved control of printed works away from publishers and gave authors legal rights over their writing.
events.significance: It is widely seen as the foundation of modern copyright law. It established the idea that authors own their creative work.

events.title: Mount Tambora erupts
events.description: Mount Tambora on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa began its colossal eruption. Ash fell across several islands.
events.significance: It was one of the most powerful eruptions in recorded history. It helped cause the 1816 'Year Without a Summer', with crop failures and food shortages across the Northern Hemisphere.

events.title: USS Thresher is lost at sea
events.description: The US Navy nuclear submarine USS Thresher sank during deep-diving tests in the Atlantic. All 129 officers, crew and civilian technicians aboard died.
events.significance: It was the first nuclear submarine lost at sea. The tragedy led to the SUBSAFE program, which greatly tightened submarine safety standards.

events.title: The Good Friday Agreement is reached
events.description: After marathon talks in Belfast, the British and Irish governments and most Northern Ireland political parties agreed a landmark peace settlement.
events.significance: The agreement largely ended the decades of violence known as the Troubles. It set up power-sharing institutions in Northern Ireland.
